newsitem.title: USA: Salomon's Shulman sees rough week for U.S. stocks.
newsitem.headline: Salomon's Shulman sees rough week for U.S. stocks.

text.p: U.S. stocks will renew their downtrend next week as a batch of economic data leads investors to again focus on rising interest rates, Salomon Brothers chief equity strategist David Shulman said on Wednesday.
U.S. blue chips have rebounded sharply in the past week, boosted by a string of strong earnings reports.
"Next week, when the focus shifts from earnings, I think the market is going to go down," Shulman said in an interview.
Shulman noted economic data coming next week including the first quarter Employment Cost Index on April 29, first quarter Gross Domestic Product on April 30 and April jobs data on Friday May 2.
He said he saw the Fed funds rate moving toward six percent and the long bond toward 7.5 percent. "That's not going to be friendly for stocks," he said.
The Federal Reserve raised its Fed funds target by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent on March 25. The 30-year Treasury bond was off 15/32 to yield 7.08 percent Wednesday.
Shulman said he expected the Dow to break its low for the year, set on a closing basis at 6392 on April 11, and move to 6000-6200, although not necessarily next week.
The Dow was off 25 at 6809 on Wednesday afternoon.
"I don't think the correction is over," he said.
